problem_statement: A DTLS server socket can only maintain a single client session at a time: it keeps one TLS/DTLS context per socket file descriptor, so a second peer connecting to the same server socket cannot establish its own handshake, and traffic from multiple peers is not routed independently. A DTLS server socket should be able to handle several clients concurrently, maintaining a separate TLS session per peer (identified by host:port, or by DTLS connection ID when used), so that each peer's handshake and data are processed on its own session; sending to and receiving from each peer via the same server socket must reach the right client, and one client closing or timing out must not disturb the other client's session.
twister_command: scripts/twister -p qemu_x86 -T tests/net/socket/tls -s tests/net/socket/tls/net.socket.tls -s net.socket.tls -O twister-out --no-clean -W
